## Requirements (contract § In scope — deliverables)

1. Public builds emit no internal routes: `web/src/pages/{curate,releases,
   research-dossier,contribution-back,visual-language}` moved to
   `web/src/internal/`, injected by the `sigInternalRoutes` Astro
   integration only under `SIG_BUILD_INTERNAL=1` (e2e + `check:perf` set
   it; a publishable build never does).
2. A committed allow-list `ops/public_routes.toml` (data, not code):
   `[allowlist].top_level` names every publishable top-level entry;
   `[allowlist].required` the subset every build must emit; `[[denied]]`
   the six never-public routes. The publish exits non-zero on any unlisted
   top-level entry or a missing required one.
3. Content assertions: refuse `data-testid="curate-auth-banner"`, form
   actions on loopback hosts (127.0.0.1 / localhost / 0.0.0.0 / ::1),
   `demo_` path segments, `demo_` hrefs, rendered `demo_` task-field ids.
4. Release record `dist/.sig-release.json`
   (`sig/web-release-record/1.0.0`): release id, git commit, build time,
   `sha256:` tree digest over the synced tree except the record itself,
   `image_digests`, `data_release`, bucket, allow-list path, publisher.
5. One command `sig-ops publish-web` (dry-run default, `--apply` to
   mutate): prepare → assertions → record → one sync → post-sync verify.
   The site sync never deletes `r/`, `releases/`, `entity/`, `conf/` or the
   release-pipeline root objects (`compat_index.json`, `release.json`) —
   `plan_site_sync` excludes them from `deletes` (reported as
   `protected_kept`) and `is_protected_object` re-checks every delete at
   the write. A staged `--release-tree` (restricted to release namespaces)
   and the public-compartment `--public-tree` sync append-only in the same
   run. `deploy.py` names `publish-web` for the public buckets;
   `ops/README.md` forbids hand-typed syncs to public buckets.
6. Absence probes: `http-absent` probe kind (`observe.http_absent` +
   `probe_hosted`), green iff exactly 404 — 200/3xx/403 = "present",
   unreachable = failure. `ops/cadence.toml` carries 18 targets (6 denied
   routes × 3 origins: apex `surveillancegraph.org`, `$SIG_PROBE_WEB_URL`,
   `storage.googleapis.com/{project}-sig-web`); `--apply` refuses when no
   probe resolves or any denied route answers non-404; the 6-hourly sweep
   picks the same rows up.
7. Regression tests (G1 §3.2 item 6): the sync refuses `curate/`, an
   unlisted top-level dir, a `demo_` page; every listed required prefix
   exists; an export-mode build without `SIG_BUILD_INTERNAL` emits no
   `curate/`; every denied route has an `http-absent` probe on every
   public origin.

Out of scope (not implemented): the release tool (P35.53), serving
topology/LB path rules (P34.40), the republish itself (P34.17 L2).

## Plan

Root cause (S0 F-02, G1 §3.2): the 2026-09-27 republish ran a hand-typed
`gcloud storage rsync -r --delete-unmatched-destination-objects` that
bypassed every build exclusion, re-published `/curate/**`, and nothing
verified the denied routes afterwards because no probe could express
"must be absent".

Approach — one repository-owned path with defence in depth:

1. Build side: move internal/withdrawn Astro sources to
   `web/src/internal/`; `sigInternalRoutes` integration injects them only
   when `SIG_BUILD_INTERNAL=1`. `strip_non_public_web` stays as
   belt-and-suspenders over a build run with the flag set.
2. Policy side: `ops/public_routes.toml` is the committed allow-list;
   `load_allowlist` fails closed on a missing/empty file and refuses a
   nonexistent *explicit* path rather than substituting the default.
3. Content side: `assert_public_tree_content` scans markup and path
   segments for internal-layout, loopback-write and demo markers.
4. Record side: `write_release_record` pins the tree digest before sync.
5. Sync side: `sync_tree` is the one sync primitive over the injectable
   `GcsBucket` (`delete_object` added for exactly this caller); site sync
   deletes remote extras minus protected namespaces; release/public trees
   are append-only.
6. Verify side: `http-absent` probes in `ops/cadence.toml` on every public
   origin run at-once post-sync (and 6-hourly by `sig-probe`); `deploy.py`
   + `ops/README.md` route operators away from hand rsync.
7. All remote-mutation guards sit before the first `put_object` — bucket,
   export bucket and the absence-verify callable are validated up front so
   a refused publish never leaves a partial sync.
